explanation: Companies raise money by selling shares of ownership called [[kw:stock]].
[[kw:Common stock]] gives voting rights and the potential for higher dividends when the company is profitable.
[[kw:Preferred stock]] usually does not carry voting rights but has priority over common stock in dividends and assets if the company is liquidated.
[[kw:Cumulative preferred stock]] requires that all unpaid past dividends ([[kw:dividends in arrears]]) be paid before common stockholders receive any dividends.

visuals.title: Interpreting Chewy (CHWY) Stock Quote
visuals.caption: Quotes can be found in newspapers or online financial sites.

explanation: A [[kw:stock quotation]] provides key information about a stock's trading activity.
[[kw:52‑week high/low]] – the highest and lowest prices in the past year.
[[kw:Stock yield]] = Annual dividend per share ÷ Last price per share × 100.
[[kw:PE ratio]] = Last price per share ÷ Annual earnings per share. It indicates how much investors are willing to pay per dollar of earnings.
[[kw:Last price]] is the closing price for the day; [[kw:net change]] is the price change from the previous day's close.
[[imp:A high PE ratio may indicate high growth expectations, while a low PE may suggest undervaluation.]]

formulaCard.title: Key Stock Quote Formulas
notes: If the PE ratio is '...', the company has no earnings.
Yield is based on the current stock price, not the purchase price.
formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Stock Yield} = \frac{\text{Annual Dividend per Share}}{\text{Last Price per Share}} \times 100$$ $$\text{Earnings per Share (EPS)} = \frac{\text{Last Price}}{\text{PE Ratio}}$$ $$\text{PE Ratio} = \frac{\text{Last Price}}{\text{EPS}}$$

confusionCorner.body: Yield is based on the current market price, not the price you paid. [[imp:Your personal return on investment depends on your purchase price, not the quote's yield.]]

explanation: When a company pays dividends, the order is: 1. Pay any [[kw:dividends in arrears]] on cumulative preferred stock. 2. Pay the current year's preferred dividend. 3. Distribute the remaining amount to common stockholders.
Preferred dividend per share is fixed (e.g., $0.80). Common dividend per share = Total remaining for common ÷ Number of common shares.
If the total dividends declared are not enough to cover preferred dividends, common stockholders receive nothing.
[[imp:Preferred stockholders do not share in extra profits beyond their fixed dividend.]]

formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Preferred Arrears} = \text{Shares} \times \text{Dividend Rate} \times \text{Years Missed}$$ $$\text{Total Preferred} = \text{Arrears} + \text{Current Year Preferred}$$ $$\text{Common Dividend per Share} = \frac{\text{Total Declared} - \text{Total Preferred}}{\text{Common Shares}}$$
notes: If total dividends are less than total preferred, common receives nothing.
Preferred dividend rate is per share per year.

examples.title: A – Compute ROI
B – ROI vs yield
examples.prompt: Explain the difference between ROI and stock yield.
steps: Yield is based only on dividends relative to the current market price.
ROI includes both dividends and capital gains relative to your original investment.
ROI is a more complete measure of your personal return.

examples.prompt: Buy 200 shares at $15, sell at $12. Buy commission $25, sell commission $25. Dividends $0.50 per share. Find ROI.
examples.title: C – Loss scenario

teacherCues: Explain that total return = dividends + capital gain (or loss).

discoveryHook.scenario: You buy 100 shares of a stock at $20 per share, paying $20 commission. Your total cost = $2,020. A year later, you sell at $25 per share (minus $20 commission) and received $1 per share in dividends. Your total return = ($2,500 – $2,020) + $100 = $580. ROI = ($580 / $2,020) × 100 ≈ 28.7%.

explanation: [[kw:Return on investment (ROI)]] measures the percentage gain or loss on an investment.
Total return = (Selling price – Purchase price) × Shares + Dividends received – Commissions.
Total cost = Purchase price × Shares + Commissions.
$$\text{ROI} = \frac{\text{Total Return}}{\text{Total Cost}} \times 100$$
[[imp:ROI accounts for both price appreciation and dividends.]]

formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Total Return} = (\text{Selling Price} - \text{Purchase Price}) \times \text{Shares} + \text{Dividends} - \text{Commissions}$$ $$\text{Total Cost} = \text{Purchase Price} \times \text{Shares} + \text{Buy Commission}$$ $$\text{ROI} = \frac{\text{Total Return}}{\text{Total Cost}} \times 100$$
notes: Commissions on both buy and sell sides are included.
If the stock is not sold, ROI can be calculated based on current market price.
formulaCard.title: Return on Investment (ROI)

teacherCues: Use the blueprint: Understand → Solve → Conclude.
Work through a problem that combines stock quotes, dividends, and ROI.

visuals.title: Blueprint: Stock Investment
visuals.caption: Always include commissions in total cost and proceeds.

rows.1: Buy 200 sh @ $18, comm $25, div $0.40/sh, sell @ $22, comm $25.

notes: If dividends are not paid, that term is zero.
PE ratio and EPS can be found from the quote data.
formulaCard.title: Stocks Blueprint
formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Total Cost} = \text{Shares} \times \text{Purchase Price} + \text{Buy Commission}$$ $$\text{Dividends} = \text{Shares} \times \text{Annual Dividend per Share}$$ $$\text{Proceeds} = \text{Shares} \times \text{Selling Price} - \text{Sell Commission}$$ $$\text{Total Return} = \text{Proceeds} - \text{Total Cost} + \text{Dividends}$$ $$\text{ROI} = \frac{\text{Total Return}}{\text{Total Cost}} \times 100$$

explanation: Apply the blueprint to stock problems:
1. Understand: identify purchase price, number of shares, commissions, dividends, selling price, and any quote data (PE, yield).
2. Solve: compute total cost, dividends, total return, ROI. If PE and price are given, find EPS or vice versa.
3. Conclude: state ROI and other requested values; evaluate whether the investment was profitable.
This structured approach ensures you account for all costs.
